headline_tag: uptrend intact, but price is still pausing below its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is solid, and this is the kind of phase in which spending to win new and returning users has historically paid back best, especially among active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price has now spent eight days just under its 50-day average, the Fed leaned slightly tougher yesterday and the US elections are next week, the sensible way to apply it is in steps: add spend gradually, review weekly, and speed up once price wins back about $81,965. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC is about 11% above its 200-day average ($73,124), which is still rising.
Up about 29% over 90 days; about 80% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But price ($81,092) has closed under its 50-day average ($81,965) for eight days.
The Fed held rates but two officials voted for a rise; price swings remain very calm.
watch: Price swings are about as calm as they have been in years while close to two bets on a rise are open for every bet on a fall, and the latest daily reading shows about $487 million leaving the US Bitcoin funds. A close back above $81,965 would ease that tension; a close below $80,151 would turn the week down, and below $74,903 a drop signal would start.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still points up, but the last week has stayed soft. Short term, the picture is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed below its 50-day average for eight days (about 1% under it) and sits about 6% below its 30-day high, while the mood reading is a flat 51 and day-to-day swings are among the calmest in years. A close above $81,965 (the 50-day average) turns the week clearly up, a close below $80,151 (the 30-day low) turns it down, and in between it stays choppy, inside a typical week's swing of about $2,700. Three newly found flaws in Bitcoin's main software were reported with fixes already released (PANews), a small safety note rather than a market event; hold big pushes until price breaks out of this zone.

Over the next month, the read is mixed. The three-month numbers still look good, with price about 29% above three months ago and about four in five of the last 90 days closing above the long-term average, but the last few weeks have faded: price is down about 3% over 30 days and CryptoQuant reports October is on track for a loss of about 4% (via PANews). News is nudging this down a little, as the Fed kept rates unchanged yesterday but two officials voted for a rise (PANews), and the US midterm elections follow on 3 November. Price must win back $81,965 (the 50-day average) before the month leans up again, with room to climb above $86,603 (the 90-day high); winning back that line would be the cue to time bigger campaigns.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 11% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about 35% below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a late-stage run; on the long-run side, Thailand's Supreme Court ruled that Bitcoin counts as legal property (PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,124 (the 200-day average), with $67,018 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. A close back under the 200-day average would weaken this read and argue for slowing spend on new users.
